## Implementation Plan

Implementation Plan
Objective: Build a complete multi-file Python library for decoding an untrusted framed binary telemetry stream arriving in arbitrarily sized chunks. Frames have a two-byte sync marker, version, flags, stream id, sequence number, payload length, payload, and CRC32. The decoder must resynchronize after noise, corrupted lengths, CRC failures, unknown versions, duplicate frames, and truncated input without quadratic scanning or unbounded buffering. Support optional zlib-compressed payloads with strict decompressed-size limits, per-stream sequence gap reporting, configurable maximum frame and buffer sizes, backpressure-friendly incremental feed/drain APIs, immutable typed events, and counters for every rejection reason. Never deserialize executable objects. Include an encoder used for round-trip tests, deterministic fuzz/property-style tests without third-party packages, adversarial one-byte chunk tests, multiple interleaved streams, wraparound sequence numbers, cancellation, and proof that retained memory remains bounded during megabytes of hostile input. Generate focused modules using only the standard library. Do not modify live project files; build and execute solely in a disposable workspace. Return all generated code, exact planning decisions, test and repair logs, per-stage timings, and a requirement coverage matrix.

  - algorithm: Initialize decoder with max_frame_size and max_buffer_size -> Iterate through input bytes in chunks -> Detect sync marker to identify frame boundaries -> Parse frame header (version, flags, stream id, sequence number, payload length) -> Verify CRC32 for data integrity -> Decompress payload if zlib-compressed -> Validate decompressed size against limits -> Store valid frames in buffer -> Recover from errors by resynchronizing and discarding invalid frames
